chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
In the month of Ramadan: 'It is a month among the months, and it is subject to the same deficiency (shortening of days) that affects other months.'
ai.seo_question: Is Ramadan subject to the same time variations as other months?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Ramadan, like all lunar months, is subject to the natural variation of 29 or 30 days, a concept known as *nuqsan* (deficiency or shortening). This establishes the astronomical basis for the Islamic calendar's flexibility, distinguishing the month's fixed religious status from its variable temporal length. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on observing the moon's actual cycle rather than adhering to a rigid, fixed 30-day count for every month.
